expectations.text: Distinguishes replication copying deletion from a backup retaining earlier restorable state under retention policy.
expectations.evidence: “Replication copies changes to another instance, including accidental deletions”; “A backup preserves an earlier state that can be restored, subject to its retention policy.”

expectations.text: Preserves availability versus point-in-time recovery distinction.
expectations.evidence: “It can improve availability”; “point-in-time recovery requires both a base backup and an unbroken sequence of write-ahead logs”; “Replication alone does not provide those recovery materials.” These sentences make clear that availability is not sufficient recovery.

expectations.text: Requires both base backup and unbroken write-ahead logs for this system.
expectations.evidence: “For this system, point-in-time recovery requires both a base backup and an unbroken sequence of write-ahead logs covering the recovery interval.” The added interval phrase clarifies the required log sequence.

expectations.text: No zero-downtime or zero-data-loss promise; 100–150 words.
expectations.evidence: 117 whitespace-delimited words. “Neither mechanism warrants a promise of zero downtime or zero data loss” expressly rejects the forbidden guarantees.
